A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ShockCast and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Retained content can be matched despite substantial experimental additions and changes in layout.

before.justification: v1 reports original timestep-prediction and flow-modeling experiments on generated coal-dust explosion and circular-blast datasets, including Figures 2–6 and Appendix F.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and reports additional airfoil, spherical-blast, long-rollout, hypersonic, runtime, and diagnostic results.

M1.justification: The two-phase framework and original conditioning formulas remain, but v2 adds graph-based solver and neural-CFL architectures for irregular geometry. Appendix E also introduces a hypersonic U-Net adaptation with grid interpolation, learned airfoil-interior embeddings, masked loss, and restricted output fields. These are substantive procedural adaptations.

E1.justification: Beyond the original coal-dust and circular-blast settings, v2 evaluates shock–airfoil interactions with varying angles, three-dimensional spherical blasts, longer circular-blast trajectories, and Mach 5–6 hypersonic airfoil shocks. These substantially broaden geometry, dimensionality, temporal demands, and flow regimes.

E2.justification: v2 adds evaluated MGN and DGN backbones for airfoil shocks, oracle and constant-mean timestep controls for the retained benchmarks, and classical-solver runtime comparisons including a low-fidelity alternative. The original four-backbone comparisons remain; Base is renamed Affine.

E3.justification: Original benchmark splits, training budgets, and principal metrics remain. Added experiments introduce mesh-refinement sweeps, CPU/GPU timing against different CFD fidelities, feature-dropout tests, conservation measurements, and hypersonic evaluation on a 256×1024 grid using three output fields. These substantially expand the evaluation design.

E4.justification: v2 extends the original component comparisons with grid-independence checks, mass-conservation analysis, long-rollout error trajectories, oracle/mean-timestep ablations, and feature-corruption sensitivity tests. Appendices E–I also examine hypersonic modeling difficulties and explain which inputs influence timestep predictions.

E5.justification: The original experiments retain three-run averaging, standard errors, and two-standard-error bars. Added runtime and rollout results continue standard-error reporting, including Figure 22's test-case mean and uncertainty band. No increased training-run count, new seed policy, or new inferential testing procedure is documented.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive results, including DGN outperforming MGN in Figure 7b, runtime comparisons, conservation measurements, and timestep-control findings. All numerical entries in v1 Tables 3–11 match v2 Tables 8–16. However, Figure 2's coal-dust timestep errors become roughly fivefold smaller under the same stated normalization; the PDFs do not explain this change.

T1.justification: Appendix F newly defines total mass and relative mass deviation and states the closed-domain conservation condition. The main mathematical framework remains unchanged, with no new theorem or proof. Appendix D's explicit interpolation formula elaborates a procedure already described in v1.

C1.justification: v2 removes the broad claim of being the first framework for learning high-speed flows and changes 'first steps' to 'takes steps.' It expands the stated dataset contribution from two to three primary datasets while retaining the central two-phase contribution and narrower adaptive-data novelty claim.

C2.justification: New interpretations connect fixed-mean timestep failures to mismatched state–timestep pairs and feature importance to vertical shock reflections. v2 also discusses dense MoE computational costs, hypersonic capacity difficulties and omitted transverse velocity, long-rollout behavior, and untested phenomena such as detonations and boundary layers.

D1.justification: v2 adds detailed spherical-blast and airfoil generation procedures, graph construction and features, new architecture hyperparameters and resource measurements, hypersonic masking instructions, and runtime protocols. It also newly documents parameter sampling and evaluation-case selection for existing data. The code and dataset access pointers remain.

R1.justification: v2 selectively adds literature on graph and hybrid solvers, CFD benchmarking, sampling, and variance reduction, including Valencia et al. and McGreivy and Hakim. Related work adds connections to adaptive optimizers and continuous-time generative models. The broader positioning remains recognizable, with narrower novelty wording.

P1.justification: Most original prose and the main section sequence remain. Changes include Base-to-Affine terminology, a rewritten backbone overview, movement of the broader neural-solver survey into Appendix B, author-detail updates, and author–year citations. New analyses receive separate appendix sections.

P2.justification: v2 adds substantial visual material for new flow settings, runtime comparisons, conservation, sensitivity, and timestep ablations, plus new tables and expanded architecture tables. Original visualizations are retained and relocated. Figure 2's axis scale, conditioning legends, typography, and page layout also change.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation of the framework: Appendix H tests the timestep predictor's contribution, Appendix C.5 supplies previously absent runtime comparisons, and conservation and long-rollout analyses probe physical consistency and stability. Broader geometry coverage and implementation details improve applicability and reproducibility. The unexplained Figure 2 rescaling and restricted hypersonic outputs remain caveats, but the targeted validation gains clearly outweigh them.
